paper.title: Your Code Agent Can Grow Alongside You with Structured Memory
paper.central_claim: MemCoder: structuring a repository's historical human commits into agent-friendly memory, retrieving it with a dual-stage retriever, refining execution with a test-writing Refining Sub-agent, and internalizing human-validated solutions into long-term memory enables continual human-AI co-evolution and reaches SOTA on SWE-bench Verified (DeepSeek-V3.2 68.4% to 77.8%).

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

sections_read: Opus: pinned text read before opening seat records (abstract, method, experiments, every table and appendix present in the pinned text) ; targeted re-reads for every disputed field

evidence.quote: MemCoder first structures historical human experience to distill latent intent-to-code mappings from past commits. It then employs a self-refinement mechanism driven by verification feedback to correct agent behavior in real-time. Crucially, an experience self-internalization mechanism is introduced to crystallize human-validated solutions into long-term knowledge, thereby supporting sustained evolution.

signatures.object: Long-term memory M of structured commit entries (keywords, problem, root cause, solution); baseline: no memory or raw commits
signatures.information: Repository commit messages and diffs (human-authored), test-time issue text; temporal cutoff before each issue
signatures.operation: LLM structures each commit into a sextuple; ANN search plus cross-encoder rerank; agent chooses when to call retrieval and with which query
signatures.output: Retrieved entries injected into the primary agent context
signatures.conditions: top-k chosen by agent with progressive schedule (prompt: initial 8, then n*8)
signatures.feedback: None for construction (human history); verification feedback only in-episode
signatures.selection_rule_data: Reranker score only; no utility-based admission
signatures.persistence: Vector DB; new commits synchronised at Stage 1
signatures.claimed_effect: w/o CR 71.6 vs 77.8; raw vs structured memory 73.0 vs 76.4
signatures.failure_boundary: top-k too large dilutes context; plateau reported

signatures.object: Refining Sub-agent output (test code and verification checklist), in-episode only
signatures.information: Problem, trajectory, environment feedback, retrieved precedents
signatures.operation: LLM writes reproduction tests and a checklist, executes them, returns result to primary agent
signatures.output: Checklist and test result in context
signatures.persistence: None; memory not modified during execution

signatures.object: Memory update by self-internalization of human-reviewed agent solutions
signatures.operation: Commit then re-ingest at next sync (set union)
signatures.failure_boundary: No dedup, conflict, retirement, or error-propagation analysis

gap.author_gap: Code agents operate on static snapshots, ignore human defect-repair history in version control and discard human-verified solutions.
gap.checked_gap: Using commit history as retrieved precedent is a real but well-trodden fixed object; the specific remaining bottleneck (agent-friendly structuring and verifiable refinement) is partly supported by Table 2, while the internalization gap is not tested.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Cited: MemoryBank, SAGE, RAPTOR, MemWalker, A-mem, MemInsight, APE, OPRO, ReAct, Self-Refine (paper Sec 2, v1). Not discussed (our_inference, not verified here): other experience-memory methods built specifically for SWE-bench agents and repository-history retrieval work.
gap.residue: How a code agent's own verified fixes should be admitted, merged and retired.
gap.stakes: Repeated errors and loss of tacit repository conventions; shown only through resolved-rate gain from retrieval.
gap.method_response: Structured commit memory, agent-driven retrieval, test-writing refinement, human-reviewed write-back.
gap.remaining_gap: Write-back loop untested; no gate, conflict or retirement; memory source is human commits rather than agent feedback.
unresolved: effect of internalization over a task stream

assessment.evidence_level_note: Opus shared correction (both seats 'retained'). The evaluated memory contains only LLM-structured human commits made before each issue (opus:O01). No agent-produced, human-validated entry is written and later reused in any experiment (opus:O02). The gains come from a non-weight retrieval component (in scope, B-class), but the ladder's 'retained' requires a retained system change that improves later tasks, and none is evaluated.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Single-run, author-reported SWE-bench Verified gains on DeepSeek-V3.2 (68.4→77.8, 342→389 of 500) from retrieving LLM-structured, time-restricted repository commit history plus a test-writing refining sub-agent. Structured beats raw commits (73.0→76.4). The self-internalization / co-evolution loop is untested, and SOTA comparability is not established (mixed pass@k, copied baselines).
unresolved: Any stream experiment of write-back (internalization) effects.
Enforcement of the temporal cutoff; backbone contamination.
top-k default chosen on a test subset (opus:O03, opus:O04).
Matched-attempt baselines; tokens/calls; Figures 3–5 values image-only.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Repository history as a source of tacit conventions is a real, named fixed object. Neighbours cited are mostly generic memory work (A-mem, MemInsight, MemoryBank), SWE-specific experience-memory lines are not compared, and the internalization gap rests on no measured failure.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. The tested chain (commit → LLM sextuple → k+p index → agent-issued dual-stage retrieval → test-writing refiner) is concrete. Raw vs structured gives a discriminating prediction (son55:E009). But the domain's M criterion is the feedback → candidate → accept → write-back → reuse chain. Here the knowledge source is human commits, not the agent's own execution feedback (son55:E017), and write-back is a bare set union after an unspecified human review (son55:E006, son55:E014), with no admission or error control. The loop that carries the central co-evolution claim is the weakest part. sol's 3 credits the retrieval pipeline's reconstructability.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The retrieval pipeline, Algorithm 1 and the full Refining prompt are reconstructable. The write-back gate, merge/conflict/retirement, versioning, human-review protocol and hyperparameters are absent, and next-run use is never traced.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Resolution comes from official SWE-bench tests via sb-cli (son55:E015), and every reported percentage matches its count out of 500 (389, 394, 419, 382, 365, 358, 342). The generated-test verifier is internal only; leaderboard pass@k mixing is a causality matter.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Cumulative ablations and the none/raw/structured comparison isolate retrieval and structuring (son55:E007, son55:E009). The evolution claim has no test, baselines are copied pass@3 numbers (son55:E010), there are no alternative memory/retrieval methods, and refiner/retrieval calls are unmatched.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked with an Opus addition. A temporal restriction to commits before each issue is stated (opus:O01) but not audited. The default initial top-k=8 (opus:O03) sits at the knee of a sweep run on a 200-issue subset of the same test set (opus:O04), so the selection set overlaps the test set (precedent r12b ARISE: anchor 2). Backbone contamination is unexamined.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder). Instance counts and negative top-k boundaries are reported. There is a single pass@1 run with no intervals, and the DSR effect is 7/500.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Retrieval frequency and retrieved-entry counts are measured on a 200-issue sweep (Fig. 4, image-only values). There is no token, dollar or latency figure, no memory-construction or human-review cost, and no matched-attempt baselines.
